checks: The mixed trace is a finite disjoint union of compact convex fibers, so q is an integer maximum affine dimension. Positive q implies no atom at y and activates the declared angular lemma.
The map s to (v,s)/||(v,s)|| is injective on each Borel ray stratum; the pullback weights k^q are Hausdorff scaling in the physical fiber and do not require a spherical Jacobian.

Interpolation with the actual center gives nested A_k and B_k. Equal positive measures force the two relative q-planes to coincide. Prefix sums are strictly increasing even when later members have zero q-area, so every positive mirrored pair is recovered almost everywhere, then exactly by relative convexity and closedness.

A reflected positive pair gives a q-dimensional Minkowski midpoint about c inside the own fiber. If no positive fiber is off-center, its positivity is automatic. Intrinsic polar integration in the own direction space is valid also at a boundary center and for q=1.

Integer-base reflection preserves the lattice and Hausdorff measure. Full retained mass gives equality of the two restricted measures. The q=0 witness has left/right counting masses 2 and 3 at y=1 and lacks the reflected partner of 3.
The frozen content matches b90a2673d60a00b3 items 1–4 and §§3–6, including the allowance for unmatched null fibers.

dependencies.hypotheses: Same-wave lemma applies with N=n+d, finite positive Hausdorff measure and no center atom because q>0. Its angular equivalence is the first two items and it gives exact depth.

overlap.comparison: The symmetric-kernel estimate gives half depth when the reflected intersection retains all ordinary d-volume. It supplies one implication at q=d and does not prove the half-depth rigidity converse, ray reconstruction, or lower-dimensional measured-fiber statements.

readability: The statement distinguishes exact equality of positive fibers from equality of the entire mixed trace.
review_method: Independent cold read of the exact frozen statement and proof, then source and predecessor comparison and exact arithmetic checks where relevant.
summary: The angular equivalence lifts to exact symmetry of all measured fibers by convex nesting on primitive base rays and polar integration in the own fiber.
